text:
incident-bot: PAGER -> high error rate and latency spike on /v1/generate (hosted-prod) — incident-id: INC-2026-0314-07. Severity: page. See /incidents/INC-2026-0314-07 for context.
Alice Nguyen: I'm on primary for the next hour, taking this. Observed 5xx + token-generation latency > 3s from multiple regions.
Jamal Rivera: I'm secondary. If you need me to take over or escalate to runtime team, ping me.
Alice Nguyen: Quick triage: checking model pool health and GPU memory OOMs. Starting by tailing runtime logs.
Alice Nguyen: logs:```
2026-03-14T07:02:03Z runtime: kv_cache_miss for model: redwood-large-8bit
2026-03-14T07:02:05Z scheduler: enqueue_delay 1200ms
2026-03-14T07:02:06Z infer: cuda out of memory on worker-3
```
Priya Patel: If it's OOM on worker-3, we can evict large KV caches temporarily. Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/runbook-gpu-oom (see 'evict-caches' step).
Alice Nguyen: Good call — running evict-caches for pod worker-3 now. Command:```bash
./infractl evict-cache --node worker-3 --model redwood-large-8bit --confirm
```
Rob Chen: Also checking autoscaler logs and pool saturation. If autoscaler is stuck, we should trigger manual scale up of dedicated pool. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/autoscale-manual-scale
Jamal Rivera: Noting customer impact: a handful of requests hit 5xx in EU region (customer-facing). Opening post-incident note.
Alice Nguyen: Evict completed, restarting worker-3 process (graceful restart). Command:```bash
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-worker-3 -n hosted-prod
```
incident-bot: Deploy bot detected restart started for runtime-worker-3 by Alice Nguyen at 2026-03-14T07:06:12Z.
Alice Nguyen: Restarted — warming up KV cache. Observed latency returning to baseline for 90% of requests.
Priya Patel: If latency persists for long-tail, switch to fallback smaller model for latency-sensitive routes. Quick config: route /v1/generate?profile=low-latency -> redwood-medium-quant. See routing-runbook: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/routing-fallbacks
Jamal Rivera: I'm going to notify support and add a short customer note: 'Transient slowdown affecting some requests in EU, mitigation in progress, no data loss.' Can someone confirm SLA impact?
Rob Chen: No request data lost, only increased latency and some 5xx. SLA calc: within minor incident threshold.
Alice Nguyen: Handoff plan — I'm primary until 07:30 UTC, then Jamal takes over. Coverage gap flagged 10:00-11:00 PST (no on-site backup) — Priya, can you cover that window remotely?
Priya Patel: I can cover remote for the 10:00-11:00 PST window. If anything escalates beyond runbook steps, page runtime team.
Jamal Rivera: Noted — will pick up at 07:30. I'll add runbook quick-links to the shift note:
- GPU OOM / evict caches: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/runbook-gpu-oom
- Manual scale autoscaler: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/autoscale-manual-scale
- Fallback routing: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/routing-fallbacks
- KV cache flush: https://wiki.redwood.com/runbooks/kv-cache-flush
Alice Nguyen: Final checks: confirm worker-3 steady at 0 OOMs for 5m, no further 5xx spike. If spike returns, set traffic to fallback and open full incident bridge.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0314-07 updated: mitigation applied (evict cache + restart). Status -> monitoring. Pager closed from active->monitoring at 2026-03-14T07:12:03Z.
Rob Chen: Adding a note to the runbook: consider automating pre-evict when enqueue_delay > 800ms for that model. I'll open a follow-up ticket.
Alice Nguyen: Thanks team. Handing off to Jamal at 07:30 UTC. Leaving the remaining check items in the shift note. :white_check_mark:
Jamal Rivera: Thanks — I'll monitor for the next hour and escalate if anything resurfaces.
Priya Patel: Good recovery. I'll prepare a short blameless postmortem template for incident author.
Alice Nguyen: closing thread, saving runbook links in the rotation doc.
